title: Data for Cases Directed to Community Mediation Centre and Community Disputes Resolution Tribunals
what_it_is: Data for Cases Directed to Community Mediation Centre and Community Disputes Resolution Tribunals

sections.label: Neighbour dispute violence and mediation
sections.summary: Asked the Minister for Law for numbers of neighbour disputes escalating to injuries and fatalities, how many went to CMC and Tribunals, and preventive measures studied.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Law (a) in each of the past two years and nine months, how many cases of disputes between neighbours had escalated to violence resulting in (i) injuries and (ii) fatalities; and (b) how many of these disputes were due to be or were being processed by the (i) Community Mediation Centre and (ii) Community Disputes Resolution Tribunals; and (c) what preventive measures are being studied and considered.

sections.label: Community Disputes Management Framework enhancement
sections.summary: Last year the Community Disputes Resolution (Amendment) Act 2024 was passed, enhancing the Community Disputes Management Framework to help neighbours engage constructively.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: Last year, we enhanced our Community Disputes Management Framework (CDMF) when this House passed the Community Disputes Resolution (Amendment) Act 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: As Minister Edwin Tong explained during the Second Reading of the Act, our aim is to strengthen our community so that neighbours can constructively engage with one another, even when disagreements arise.

sections.label: Informal and formal mediation efforts
sections.summary: Community leaders and HDB officers mediate informally early and encourage residents to attempt formal mediation at the Community Mediation Centre, which is effective when both neighbours participate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: So, whenever community leaders or Housing and Development Board (HDB) officers become aware of a dispute, they attempt to mediate informally, particularly at an early stage, before relationships break down.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: They will also encourage residents to attempt formal mediation at the Community Mediation Centre (CMC).

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: When both neighbours participate, mediation has proven effective in resolving community disputes.

sections.label: Mediation directions at CMC
sections.summary: MDs are legally backed orders requiring recipients to attend mediation at the CMC.

sentences.text: MDs are legally backed orders that require recipients to attend mediation at the CMC.

sections.label: CRU and MD pilot
sections.summary: Since 7 April 2025, the CRU and the MD framework have been piloted in the HDB estates of Tampines town.

sentences.text: Since 7 April 2025, the CRU and the MD framework have been piloted in the HDB estates of Tampines town.

sections.label: CMC voluntary mediation registrations
sections.summary: From November 2024 to August 2025, about 1,300 neighbour disputes were registered with the CMC for voluntary mediation, and in about 50% one party did not respond.

sentences.text: For disputes that proceed to formal mediation, from November 2024 to August 2025, about 1,300 neighbour disputes were registered with the CMC for voluntary mediation.
In about 50% of these cases, one party did not respond.

sections.label: Mediation directions issued since April 2025
sections.summary: Since 7 April 2025, the CRU issued one MD, HDB issued none, and the CMC issued no re-mediation directions.

sentences.text: Since 7 April 2025, the CRU has issued one MD; HDB has not issued any MDs; and the CMC has not issued any re-mediation directions under the MD framework.

sections.label: CDRT enhancements for non-compliance
sections.summary: Once CDRT enhancements are operationalised, non-compliant complainants cannot file CDRT claims, and the CDRT may make adverse costs orders against non-compliant respondents.

sentences.text: First, apart from the fine mentioned earlier, once the CDRT enhancements are fully operationalised, complainants who fail to comply with an MD will not be allowed to file a CDRT claim against their neighbours.
Next, where a respondent fails to comply, and a case is subsequently filed with the CDRT, the CDRT may make an adverse costs order against the respondent.

sections.label: CMC mediation access and mediators
sections.summary: The CMC established 18 satellite mediation locations and its pool of trained volunteer mediators grew from about 140 in early 2022 to around 170 by October 2025.

sentences.text: The CMC has increased accessibility to voluntary mediation by establishing 18 satellite mediation locations at various ServiceSG Centres, Community Clubs and Neighbourhood Police Posts.
The CMC continues to expand its pool of trained volunteer mediators, which has grown from about 140 at the start of 2022, to around 170 as of October 2025.
